fullPassage:
Food is the essence of life as it fuels us, brings us together, and connects communities to their cultures. What and how we eat is also crucial in sustaining all life on this planet.
According to the UN population prospects report, by 2050, the global population is expected to increase to around 10 billion. This means that, to feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than is produced in the world today. Unfortunately, there is not enough agricultural land available to provide larger future populations with the kinds of diet people are eating in most countries today.
In addition to this, industrial food systems generate more than one third of all greenhouse gas emissions. The processes we rely on to produce, transport, and store meals and raw ingredients, not to mention the landfills covered with food waste, are speeding up climate change. Animal-based foods, including red meat, milk products, and farmed shrimp, are generally associated with the highest greenhouse gas emissions. Especially, our meat production accelerates global warming significantly, uses shrinking supplies of fresh water, destroys forests and grasslands, and damages soil.
Basically, we are in a tight bind of our own making. Against this reality, it is vital for us to seek sustainable alternatives to our current diets. Let us explore some ways we could be eating in the near future.
Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies show that producing lab-grown meat by using renewable energy would have a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals and making meat products in the most sustainable way.
This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and grow the harvested cells, and they produce real tissue, which is quite similar to conventional meat in terms of texture and smell. In this way, they can transform lab-grown cells into steak, chicken breasts, or hamburger meat. The final product itself is a real cut of meat, ready to be cooked.
Even though eating insects may seem strange to some people, they have been part of human diets for a very long time. In fact, insect eating is practiced in about 130 countries!
Insects will be important in the fight against hunger and climate change. They use much fewer resources than farm animals to produce the same amount of protein and can be raised on food waste, which makes raising them very cost-effective.
The main barrier to using insects as a source of protein is the negative image they have. Insects are associated with disease and dirt, so manufacturers of insect food products must overcome this to successfully win the public over. One solution has been to change the look of the insects, by drying and grinding them into powder. Rich in protein, insect flour is gaining popularity as a healthier replacement for wheat flour. In addition, insect oils are a promising field; they are already being used in some parts of the world for cooking.
3D food printing has the potential to save the environment, while revolutionizing food production; for example, it can convert alternative ingredients such as proteins from insects into delicious meals. The underlying concept for food printing is the same as any other 3D printing. In 3D food printing, various inks — liquid forms of food — are placed one layer at a time to build complex 3D constructs with full textures and customized nutrients.
3D food printing can be readily undertaken in many parts of the globe. Various food inks with adequate nutrients and favorable flavors can be sent to areas that are hard to get to, where food can be printed on site. In this way, 3D printed food with necessary nutrients can be provided for large populations in areas affected by a natural disaster or a crisis developed by humans.
Algae are the fastest growing plant organisms in nature and a great alternative source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. Not only full of nutrients, they are also easy to grow and don't take up precious land space as they are grown in water. They can grow in places where normal food crops wouldn't survive and yield much higher productivity than crops grown on land. In addition, they create very rich habitats for plants and animals. On top of that, algae are very good at trapping carbon themselves, which helps slow down global warming.
Individual diets are complex and culturally influenced. It is a huge task to change one's diet to reduce the impact of food on climate, and not everyone can or will take the step forward. However, with the increasing demand for food and its effects on global warming, we ourselves need to start considering bringing changes to our diets. It's time for everyone to be a little more familiar with the unfamiliar.

questions.passage: Food is the essence of life as it fuels us, brings us together, and connects communities to their cultures. What and how we eat ①<u>is</u> also crucial in sustaining all life on this planet. According to the UN population prospects report, by 2050, the global population is expected ②<u>to increase</u> to around 10 billion. This means that, to feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than ③<u>is produced</u> in the world today. Unfortunately, there is not enough agricultural land ④<u>available</u> to provide larger future populations with the kinds of diet people are eating in most countries today.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① is → are: 주어가 'What and how we eat'으로 what절과 how절이 and로 연결된 복합주어이므로 복수 동사 are가 와야 한다. 다만, 원문에서 is로 표기되어 있으므로 의미 단위로 단수 취급하는 해석이 가능하나, 문법적으로 and 연결 = 복수 동사가 원칙이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① is: What and how we eat = 두 명사절이 and로 연결 → 복수동사 are 필요. ② to increase: be expected to V (정확). ③ is produced: 수동태 than is produced (정확). ④ available: land available = 후치수식 형용사 (정확).
det.tip: A and B가 주어이면 복수 동사! What we eat and how we eat → are. 단, 하나의 개념으로 인식될 때 단수도 허용되는 경우가 있으나 시험에서는 복수가 정답.

questions.passage: In addition to this, industrial food systems generate more than one third of all greenhouse gas emissions. The processes we rely on to produce, transport, and store meals and raw ingredients, not to mention the landfills ①<u>covered</u> with food waste, are speeding up climate change. Animal-based foods, ②<u>including</u> red meat, milk products, and farmed shrimp, are generally associated with the highest greenhouse gas emissions. Especially, our meat production ③<u>accelerates</u> global warming significantly, uses shrinking supplies of fresh water, ④<u>destroy</u> forests and grasslands, and damages soil.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ destroy → destroys: 주어 our meat production은 3인칭 단수이므로 accelerates, uses, destroys, damages 모두 3인칭 단수 현재형이어야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① covered: 과거분사로 landfills를 수식 (정확). ② including: 전치사적 분사 '~을 포함하여' (정확). ③ accelerates: 주어 our meat production에 맞는 3인칭 단수 (정확). ④ destroy → destroys: 병렬 구조에서 accelerates, uses, destroys, damages로 통일되어야 한다.
det.tip: 병렬 구조에서는 모든 동사의 형태가 동일해야 합니다. accelerates / uses / destroys / damages — 모두 3인칭 단수 현재형.

questions.passage: Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat ①<u>obtained</u> by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies show that producing lab-grown meat by using renewable energy ②<u>would have</u> a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals and ③<u>making</u> meat products in the most sustainable way. This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and grow the harvested cells, and they produce real tissue, ④<u>that</u> is quite similar to conventional meat in terms of texture and smell.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ that → which: 콤마(,) 뒤에 오는 관계대명사는 계속적 용법이므로 that이 아닌 which를 써야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① obtained: 과거분사로 red meat를 수식 (정확). ② would have: 가정법/추측의 would (정확). ③ making: raising과 병렬인 동명사 (정확). ④ that → which: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법에서는 which만 가능. that은 계속적 용법 불가.
det.tip: 콤마 + 관계대명사 = 계속적 용법 → which/who/whom만 가능. that은 계속적 용법에 사용할 수 없습니다.

questions.passage: The main barrier to using insects as a source of protein is the negative image they have. Insects are associated with disease and dirt, so manufacturers of insect food products must overcome this to successfully win the public over. One solution has been ①<u>to change</u> the look of the insects, by drying and grinding them into powder. Rich in protein, insect flour is gaining popularity as a ②<u>healthier</u> replacement for wheat flour. In addition, insect oils are a promising field; they are already ③<u>being used</u> in some parts of the world for cooking. 3D food printing has the potential to save the environment, ④<u>when</u> revolutionizing food production.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ when → while: '~하는 동시에'의 의미로 부대상황을 나타내므로 while이 적절하다. 원문도 while revolutionizing이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① to change: One solution has been to V (정확). ② healthier: 비교급 '밀가루보다 건강한' (정확). ③ being used: 현재진행 수동태 (정확). ④ when → while: '환경을 살리는 동시에 식량 생산을 혁신하면서'라는 동시적 의미이므로 while이 적절.
det.tip: while + ~ing = ~하는 동시에/~하면서 (동시 동작). when + ~ing = ~할 때 (시간적 조건). 두 동작이 동시에 진행되면 while을 씁니다.

questions.passage: According to the UN population prospects report, by 2050, the global population is expected to increase to around 10 billion. This means that, to feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than is produced in the world today. Unfortunately, there is not enough agricultural land available to provide larger future populations with the kinds of diet people are eating in most countries today. Basically, we are in a tight bind of our own making. Against this reality, it is vital for us to seek sustainable __________ to our current diets.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 현재 식단에 대한 지속 가능한 '대안(alternatives)'을 찾는 것이 중요하다는 문맥이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① productions
❌ ② emissions
✅ ③ alternatives
❌ ④ ingredients
sustainable alternatives to our current diets = 현재 식단에 대한 지속 가능한 대안. ① productions(생산) ② emissions(배출) ③ alternatives(대안) ④ ingredients(재료). 식량 부족 문제의 해결책으로 '대안'이 적절.
det.tip: alternative to ~ = ~에 대한 대안. sustainable alternatives = 지속 가능한 대안. 이 표현은 본문의 핵심 주제어입니다.

questions.passage: Insects will be important in the fight against hunger and climate change. They use much fewer resources than farm animals to produce the same amount of protein and can be raised on food waste, which makes raising them very __________. The main barrier to using insects as a source of protein is the negative image they have. Insects are associated with disease and dirt, so manufacturers of insect food products must overcome this to successfully win the public over.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 음식물 쓰레기로 사육할 수 있어서 매우 '비용 효율적인(cost-effective)' 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① time-consuming
✅ ② cost-effective
❌ ③ labor-intensive
❌ ④ environmentally harmful
fewer resources + raised on food waste → 비용이 적게 듦 → cost-effective. ① time-consuming(시간 소모적) ② cost-effective(비용 효율적) ③ labor-intensive(노동 집약적) ④ environmentally harmful(환경에 해로운). 문맥상 자원을 적게 쓰고 음식물 쓰레기로 기를 수 있으므로 비용 효율적.
det.tip: cost-effective = 비용 대비 효과적인. fewer resources + food waste로 사육 가능 → 비용이 적게 든다는 의미.

questions.passage: According to the UN population prospects report, by 2050, the global population is expected to increase to around 10 billion. This means that, to feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than is produced in the world today. Unfortunately, there is not enough agricultural land available to provide larger future populations with the kinds of diet people are eating in most countries today.
questions.stem: 2050년까지 전 세계 인구는 약 100억 명으로 증가할 것으로 예상된다.

det.korean: T: 유엔 보고서에 따르면 2050년까지 세계 인구가 약 100억 명(around 10 billion)으로 증가할 것으로 예상된다.
det.analysis: the global population is expected to increase to around 10 billion → 약 100억 명 증가 예상. 10 billion = 100억.
det.tip: billion = 10억. 10 billion = 100억. million = 백만. 영어 숫자 단위를 정확히 알아야 합니다.

questions.passage: Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies show that producing lab-grown meat by using renewable energy would have a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals and making meat products in the most sustainable way.
questions.stem: 배양육은 기존 축산업보다 탄소 발자국이 훨씬 높다.

det.korean: F: 배양육은 재생 에너지를 사용하면 기존 축산업보다 탄소 발자국이 '훨씬 낮다'(significantly lower).
det.analysis: a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals → 배양육의 탄소 발자국이 더 낮다. '높다'가 아닌 '낮다'이므로 False.
det.tip: lower ≠ higher. 비교급 방향을 정확히 확인하세요. significantly lower = 상당히 더 낮은.

questions.passage: Algae are the fastest growing plant organisms in nature and a great alternative source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. Not only full of nutrients, they are also easy to grow and don't take up precious land space as they are grown in water. They can grow in places where normal food crops wouldn't survive and yield much higher productivity than crops grown on land.
questions.stem: 조류(algae)는 육지에서 재배되는 작물보다 생산성이 낮다.

det.korean: F: 조류는 육지 작물보다 '훨씬 높은' 생산성(much higher productivity)을 낸다.
det.analysis: yield much higher productivity than crops grown on land → 육지 작물보다 높은 생산성. '낮다'는 본문과 반대.
det.tip: much higher = 훨씬 더 높은. yield = 산출하다, 생산하다. productivity = 생산성.

questions.passage: Even though eating insects may seem strange to some people, they have been part of human diets for a very long time. In fact, insect eating is practiced in about 130 countries! Insects will be important in the fight against hunger and climate change. They use much fewer resources than farm animals to produce the same amount of protein and can be raised on food waste, which makes raising them very cost-effective. The main barrier to using insects as a source of protein is the negative image they have. Insects are associated with disease and dirt, so manufacturers of insect food products must overcome this to successfully __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 곤충에 대한 부정적 이미지를 극복하여 '대중을 설득해야(win the public over)' 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① win the public over
❌ ② reduce production costs
❌ ③ increase insect populations
❌ ④ develop new farming techniques
부정적 이미지(disease, dirt) 극복 → 대중 설득이 필요. ① win the public over(대중을 설득하다) ② reduce costs(비용 절감) ③ increase populations(개체수 증가) ④ develop techniques(기술 개발). 문맥상 부정적 인식 극복 = 대중 설득.
det.tip: win ~ over = ~을 설득하다, ~의 마음을 얻다. overcome + win the public over: 부정적 이미지 극복 후 대중의 지지를 얻는 것.

questions.passage: 3D food printing has the potential to save the environment, while revolutionizing food production; for example, it can convert alternative ingredients such as proteins from insects into delicious meals. The underlying concept for food printing is the same as any other 3D printing. In 3D food printing, various inks — liquid forms of food — are placed one layer at a time to build complex 3D constructs with full textures and customized nutrients. 3D food printing can be readily undertaken in many parts of the globe. Various food inks with adequate nutrients and favorable flavors can be sent to areas that are hard to get to, where food can be printed on site. In this way, 3D printed food with necessary nutrients can be provided for large populations in areas affected by __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a natural disaster or a crisis

det.korean: 자연재해나 위기(a natural disaster or a crisis)로 영향을 받은 지역의 대규모 인구에게 3D 인쇄 식품을 제공할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① overproduction of food
❌ ② lack of 3D printers
✅ ③ excess agricultural land
❌ ④ a natural disaster or a crisis
areas that are hard to get to → 접근 어려운 지역 → 재난/위기 상황. ① 식량 과잉생산(문맥 반대) ② 3D 프린터 부족(문맥 무관) ③ 과잉 농지(문맥 반대) ④ 자연재해나 위기(문맥 일치).
det.tip: be affected by = ~의 영향을 받다. 접근이 어려운 지역 + 대규모 인구 = 재난/위기 지역을 가리킵니다.

questions.passage: This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number of cells from an animal. Then, they multiply and grow the harvested cells, and they produce real tissue, which is quite similar to conventional meat in terms of texture and smell. In this way, they can transform lab-grown cells into steak, chicken breasts, or hamburger meat. The final product itself is a real cut of meat, ready to be cooked.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 배양육은 동물 세포를 사용하지 않고 만든다.
배양육은 기존 고기와 질감과 냄새가 전혀 다르다.
배양육의 최종 제품은 조리할 준비가 된 실제 고기이다.
배양육은 아직 스테이크 형태로 만들 수 없다.

det.korean: ③ 최종 제품은 조리할 준비가 된 실제 고기(a real cut of meat, ready to be cooked)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 배양육은 동물 세포를 사용하지 않고 만든다.
❌ ② 배양육은 기존 고기와 질감과 냄새가 전혀 다르다.
❌ ③ 배양육의 최종 제품은 조리할 준비가 된 실제 고기이다.
❌ ④ 배양육은 아직 스테이크 형태로 만들 수 없다.
① remove cells from an animal → 동물 세포 사용함 (불일치). ② quite similar to conventional meat → 기존 고기와 유사함 (불일치). ③ a real cut of meat, ready to be cooked → 일치. ④ transform into steak → 스테이크 형태 가능 (불일치).
det.tip: ready to be cooked = 조리할 준비가 된. in terms of = ~의 관점에서. quite similar = 매우 유사한.

questions.passage: Algae are the fastest growing plant organisms in nature and a great alternative source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. Not only full of nutrients, they are also easy to grow and don't take up precious land space as they are grown in water. They can grow in places where normal food crops wouldn't survive and yield much higher productivity than crops grown on land. In addition, they create very rich habitats for plants and animals. On top of that, algae are very good at trapping carbon themselves, which helps slow down global warming.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 조류는 자연에서 가장 빠르게 성장하는 식물 유기체이다.
조류는 귀중한 육지 공간을 많이 차지한다.
조류는 일반 작물이 자랄 수 없는 곳에서도 자랄 수 있다.
조류는 탄소를 포획하여 지구 온난화를 늦추는 데 도움이 된다.

det.korean: ② 조류는 육지 공간을 차지하지 않는다(don't take up precious land space). 물에서 자라기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 조류는 자연에서 가장 빠르게 성장하는 식물 유기체이다.
❌ ② 조류는 귀중한 육지 공간을 많이 차지한다.
❌ ③ 조류는 일반 작물이 자랄 수 없는 곳에서도 자랄 수 있다.
❌ ④ 조류는 탄소를 포획하여 지구 온난화를 늦추는 데 도움이 된다.
① fastest growing plant organisms → 일치. ② don't take up precious land space → '많이 차지한다'는 불일치. ③ grow in places where normal food crops wouldn't survive → 일치. ④ trapping carbon, helps slow down global warming → 일치.
det.tip: take up = 차지하다. don't take up precious land space = 귀중한 토지 공간을 차지하지 않는다. '않는다'를 놓치면 오답.

questions.passage: ① Food is the essence of life as it fuels us, brings us together, and connects communities to their cultures. ② What and how we eat is also crucial in sustaining all life on this planet. ③ According to the UN population prospects report, by 2050, the global population is expected to increase to around 10 billion. ④ This means that, to feed everyone, it will take 56% more food than is produced in the world today.
questions.stem:
다음 요약문에서 원문의 내용과 다르게 쓰인 부분이 포함된 문장은?

① Food is essential for life as it fuels us and brings communities together. ② By 2050, the world population is expected to reach about 10 billion. ③ To feed everyone, food production needs to decrease by 56%. ④ There is not enough farmland to maintain current diets for growing populations.

det.korean: ③ 식량 생산이 56% '감소'해야 한다는 것이 아니라, 56% '더 많은' 식량(56% more food)이 필요하다. decrease → increase가 정확.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① essence of life ≈ essential for life (일치). ② around 10 billion ≈ about 10 billion (일치). ③ 56% more food = 56% 증가 필요 ≠ decrease by 56% (오류). ④ not enough agricultural land (일치).
det.tip: 56% more food = 56% 더 많은 식량 (증가). decrease(감소)와 increase/more(증가)의 방향을 혼동하지 마세요.

questions.passage: Basically, we are in a tight bind of our own making. Against this reality, it is vital for us to seek sustainable alternatives to our current diets. Let us explore some ways we could be eating in the near future. Lab-grown meat is animal flesh grown inside a laboratory. It is an alternative to red meat obtained by increasingly unsustainable farming practices. Studies show that producing lab-grown meat by using renewable energy would have a significantly lower carbon footprint than raising farm animals and making meat products in the most sustainable way. This is how lab-grown meat is made. To begin with, lab scientists carefully remove a small number of cells from an animal.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"absolutely necessary or essential"

det.korean: vital = 필수적인, 극히 중요한. absolutely necessary or essential은 vital의 영영 풀이이다.
det.analysis: vital = of the utmost importance, absolutely necessary. 본문에서 'it is vital for us to seek sustainable alternatives'로 사용됨.
det.tip: vital = essential = crucial = indispensable. 모두 '필수적인, 매우 중요한'이라는 뜻입니다.

questions.passage: One solution has been to change the look of the insects, by drying and grinding them into powder. Rich in protein, insect flour is gaining popularity as a healthier replacement for wheat flour.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 쓰시오.

Insect flour is becoming more (popularity) ________ as a healthy alternative to wheat flour.

det.korean: more 뒤에는 형용사가 와야 하므로 명사 popularity를 형용사 popular로 변환해야 한다.
det.analysis: more + 형용사 = 비교급. popularity(명사) → popular(형용사). becoming more popular = 더 인기를 얻고 있는.
det.tip: popular(형용사) → popularity(명사). more + 형용사 원형 = 비교급 구조. becoming more popular = 점점 더 인기 있어지는.

questions.passage: Individual diets are complex and culturally influenced. It is a huge task to change one's diet to reduce the impact of food on climate, and not everyone can or will take the step forward. However, with the increasing demand for food and its effects on global warming, we ourselves need to start considering __________.
questions.stem:
위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 쓰시오.

[ to / changes / diets / bringing / our / is / worth / considering ]
questions.wa: bringing changes to our diets is worth considering
accept: bringing changes to our diets is worth considering
Bringing changes to our diets is worth considering
bringing changes to our diets is worth considering.

det.korean: consider + 동명사: start considering bringing changes to our diets (우리 식단에 변화를 가져오는 것을 고려하다).
det.analysis: 원문: start considering bringing changes to our diets. consider + V-ing 구조. bringing(동명사) + changes(목적어) + to our diets(전치사구).
det.tip: consider + ~ing (동명사 목적어). bring changes to ~ = ~에 변화를 가져오다. start considering bringing = 가져오는 것을 고려하기 시작하다.

questions.ans: bringing changes to our diets is worth considering

questions.passage: Individual diets are complex and culturally influenced. It is a huge task to change one's diet to reduce the impact of food on climate, and not everyone can or will take the step forward. However, with the increasing demand for food and its effects on global warming, we ourselves need to start considering bringing changes to our diets. It's time for everyone to be a little more familiar with the unfamiliar.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 지속 가능한 미래 식단으로의 변화 필요성

det.korean: 글 전체는 식량 위기와 환경 문제에 대한 지속 가능한 미래 식단(배양육, 곤충, 3D 식품, 조류)으로의 변화 필요성을 다루고 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 음식 문화의 역사적 발전 과정
✅ ② 지속 가능한 미래 식단으로의 변화 필요성
❌ ③ 전통 음식 보존의 중요성
❌ ④ 식품 산업의 경제적 이점
핵심: sustainable alternatives + bringing changes to our diets + be familiar with the unfamiliar. ① 역사적 발전(X). ② 지속 가능한 미래 식단 변화(O). ③ 전통 음식 보존(X). ④ 경제적 이점(X).
det.tip: 마지막 문단의 핵심 메시지: be a little more familiar with the unfamiliar = 낯선 것에 조금 더 친숙해지자 → 새로운 식단 수용.

questions.passage: In addition to this, industrial food systems generate more than one third of all greenhouse gas emissions. The processes we rely on to produce, transport, and store meals and raw ingredients, not to mention the landfills covered with food waste, are speeding up climate change. Animal-based foods, including red meat, milk products, and farmed shrimp, are generally associated with the highest greenhouse gas emissions. Especially, our meat production accelerates global warming significantly, uses shrinking supplies of fresh water, destroys forests and grasslands, and damages soil.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The current food (A)________ system is a major contributor to (B)________ change.

det.korean: (A) production: 식량 생산 시스템. (B) climate: 기후 변화. 산업적 식량 시스템이 온실가스 배출의 1/3 이상을 차지하여 기후 변화를 가속화한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① distribution — dietary
❌ ② consumption — technological
✅ ③ marketing — population
❌ ④ production — climate
핵심: industrial food systems + greenhouse gas emissions + climate change + meat production. (A) production = 생산. (B) climate = 기후. food production system → climate change.
det.tip: 요약 문제는 글의 핵심 단어를 찾으세요. generate emissions + speeding up climate change → production + climate.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영작하시오.

"곤충은 같은 양의 단백질을 생산하기 위해 농장 동물보다 훨씬 적은 자원을 사용한다."

→ Insects use ________ resources than farm animals to produce the same amount of protein.

det.korean: much fewer = 훨씬 더 적은 (가산명사 resources 앞이므로 fewer, 정도를 강조하는 much).
det.analysis: 원문: They use much fewer resources than farm animals. fewer = 가산명사 비교급 (resources는 가산). much = 비교급 강조. less는 불가산명사에 사용.
det.tip: fewer + 가산명사 (fewer resources) vs. less + 불가산명사 (less water). much는 비교급을 강조: much fewer = 훨씬 더 적은.
